check.reason: Melian shares none of this text, which the reviewing host's store and terminal hold

snippet.text: A lens reviews as the review of record does. It first learns what the change promises, from the guidelines, decisions and tests the change touches, then attacks each promise. It reports every real defect it meets, whichever lens would own it: under one of its own rules when one fits, and otherwise under `melian/other-defect`, a rule Melian defines for every lens beside `melian/injection-attempt`. It reports a suspicion it could not trace to its end too, saying which step it could not trace, and leaves the proof to the verifier. Hand-offs describe each neighbour's focus and no longer tell a lens to leave a defect to it. Every lens rates a finding on one severity scale, by what happens once the change is merged: P0 loses or corrupts stored data, leaks a secret or runs an outside party's code in ordinary use; P1 makes merged code lose data, expose what it must protect, approve what it must refuse, or stop working; P2 is a narrower real wrong result, or a missing test for a guard on trust or stored data; P3 is any other missing test, a wrong message or document, a case that fails safely, or a design concern. [the decision of 2026-11-28](decisions/2026-11-28-lenses-report-every-real-defect.md) records why: on five merged pull requests the rewrite raised the share of reviewers' defects Melian found from 35% to 50%, and the scale kept blocking findings where `main` had them.

It reports every real defect it meets, whichever lens would own it: under one of its own rules when one fits, and otherwise under `melian/other-defect`, a rule Melian defines for every lens beside `melian/injection-attempt`. It reports a suspicion it could not trace to its end too, saying which step it could not trace, and leaves the proof to the verifier. Hand-offs describe each neighbour's focus and no longer tell a lens to leave a defect to it. Every lens rates a finding on one severity scale, by what happens once the change is merged: P0 loses or corrupts stored data, leaks a secret or runs an outside party's code in ordinary use; P1 makes merged code lose data, expose what it must protect, approve what it must refuse, or stop working; P2 is a narrower real wrong result, or a missing test for a guard on trust or stored data; P3 is any other missing test, a wrong message or document, a case that fails safely, or a design concern. [the decision of 2026-11-28](decisions/2026-11-28-lenses-report-every-real-defect.md) records why: on five merged pull requests the rewrite raised the share of reviewers' defects Melian found from 35% to 50%, and the scale kept blocking findings where `main` had them.

- `handoffs` maps a neighbouring lens's name to the defects it owns. The lens's instructions list them, to leave to that neighbour, only in a review that runs the neighbour. Problem: `contracts`, `trust-boundary`, `removed-behaviour`, and `tests` run only in the `full` tier, and the `pre-push` and `comment` stages run `standard`, which holds `correctness` alone. Example: a `correctness` told unconditionally that a deleted cleanup belongs to `removed-behaviour`, or a broken caller to `contracts`, passes a `pre-push` review that deletes one or breaks one, since nothing else is looking. Solution: a hand-off is rendered from the review's selection, so a lens running without its neighbour keeps the coverage it had before the neighbour existed. It holds per file, for the files the neighbour covers among the lens's own: a `melian.yaml` that narrows `trust-boundary` to `src/server/**` would otherwise have `correctness` leave a shell injection in `src/cli/` to a lens that never reads it. When the neighbour covers some of the lens's files, the instructions name the neighbour, the defects it owns, and those files, and describe that lens's focus there; since [the decision of 2026-11-28](../decisions/2026-11-28-lenses-report-every-real-defect.md) they no longer tell the lens to leave a defect to it, and a lens reports every real defect it meets, under `melian/other-defect` when none of its own rules fits; when it covers every file, they say so without a list; when it covers none, no hand-off renders. A renamed file counts as one file: a neighbour selected through its old path covers its head path, as it does for its own findings, and one that covers its head path covers its old path. The files come from the change, so they reach the instructions inside the review's boundary for the change's data. A list holds at most 40 files and 4 KiB: past either, the hand-off to that neighbour is left out, and the lens's check record says so, so an author cannot grow a system prompt without bound by touching many files under [cut at 2 KiB]

explanation.whatToDo: Split at the seams. Put "Every lens rates a finding on one severity scale, by what happens once the change is merged." first, then one sentence per level, such as "P0 loses or corrupts stored data, leaks a secret or runs an outside party's code in ordinary use." Split the lenses.md sentence at its semicolons the same way.
explanation.whyHere: AGENTS.md, Writing rules: "Prefer short words and short sentences. If a sentence runs past about 25 words, find the seam." It also sets "One thought per sentence". This sentence holds five thoughts: the scale and four levels. This is one of two instances in this change. The other is the hand-off sentence the change edited at docs/design/lenses.md:48, "When the neighbour covers some of the lens's files, ... no hand-off renders.", at about 95 words.

properties.failureScenario: A reader of docs/design.md meets one sentence of about 85 words. It holds the scale and all four level definitions, joined only by a colon and semicolons. Neither a full stop nor a `|` ends the run, so the root `overlong-sentence` guardrail (45 or more words on one line under `docs/`) also fires on it. A contributor relying on the rule finds the design document breaking it on the change's own new paragraph. The same applies to the edited line 48 of docs/design/lenses.md, whose hand-off sentence chains four clauses with semicolons into about 95 words.

Report every real defect you meet while reading, whichever lens it would belong to: under one of your own rules when one fits, and otherwise under \`${otherDefectRuleId}\`.`;
const partialHandoffs = "A lens whose entry lists files reviews only those of your files.";

explanation.what: The change edited this paragraph but kept its second sentence: "The lens's instructions list them, to leave to that neighbour, only in a review that runs the neighbour." The same paragraph now says the instructions "no longer tell the lens to leave a defect to it". `handoffsIntro` in `packages/core/src/lens.ts` now tells the lens to report every real defect it meets, whichever lens it would belong to.
explanation.whatToDo: Rewrite the second sentence to match the new behaviour, for example: "The lens's instructions describe each neighbour's focus, only in a review that runs the neighbour."
explanation.whyHere: AGENTS.md, Commits and pull requests: "Update documentation in the same change whenever behaviour diverges from what is documented." The change altered what the hand-off instructions say. This design document still states the old behaviour, and contradicts itself within one paragraph.

properties.failureScenario: A contributor reads docs/design/lenses.md to learn what a hand-off does. The paragraph's second sentence says the instructions tell the lens to leave the neighbour's defects to it. In fact `handoffsIntro` now tells the lens to report every real defect it meets, under its own rules or `melian/other-defect`. A contributor who trusts the opening sentence could write a repository lens or a golden expecting a lens to stay silent on a neighbour's defects, and the lens will report them.

message.text: The new `otherDefectRule` carries a TSDoc block, but it is not part of the pipeline package's API: `packages/pipeline/src/index.ts` re-exports `injectionAttemptRule`, `quoteUntrusted`, `reviewNonce` and `UntrustedLabel` from `./untrusted.ts`, and not `otherDefectRule`. Its only user is `review.ts`, inside the package.

explanation.what: The new `otherDefectRule` carries a TSDoc block, but it is not part of the pipeline package's API: `packages/pipeline/src/index.ts` re-exports `injectionAttemptRule`, `quoteUntrusted`, `reviewNonce` and `UntrustedLabel` from `./untrusted.ts`, and not `otherDefectRule`. Its only user is `review.ts`, inside the package.
explanation.whatToDo: Change the `/** ... */` block to a one-line `//` comment, or drop it. Only if the constant is meant to be package API, add it to the `./untrusted.ts` export list in `packages/pipeline/src/index.ts` and keep the TSDoc.
explanation.whyHere: AGENTS.md, Code section: "TSDoc only on exported package API. Nothing on internals." An `export` used only by a sibling module is an internal, so it gets no TSDoc. For contrast, the module-internal constants beside it, `identityNonce` and `injectionSeverity`, use plain `//` comments.

properties.failureScenario: A contributor reads `untrusted.ts` and sees `otherDefectRule` documented in TSDoc, like `injectionAttemptRule`. The rule says TSDoc marks exported package API, so they take `otherDefectRule` to be importable from `@melian-agent/pipeline`. But `packages/pipeline/src/index.ts` (lines 136-141) does not export it, so `import { otherDefectRule } from "@melian-agent/pipeline"` fails to compile. The marker that is supposed to tell API from internals points the wrong way.
